title: Likes and plans
can: Say what you like and do not like, make plans with aller and a verb, and ask questions.
doneText: You can now say what you like, talk about what you are going to do, and ask a friend a question.

discover.intro: Blue sentences say what happens now. Orange sentences say what will happen. Spot how the verb changes.

groups.label: Going to do it
lines: I'm going to watch a film.

discover.question: How do the orange sentences say what is going to happen?
options: They use a form of aller (je vais) and then the infinitive: the verb ending in -er, like manger.
They add -ra to the end of the verb.
They put the verb at the end of the sentence.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Look for a new little word before the verb in each orange sentence, and look at how the verb ends.
discover.reveal: Je vais plus an infinitive means I'm going to. It is the easy way to talk about the future, and the verb after it never changes. You can also ask questions in three ways:

hooks.title: Going to
rows: He's going to watch a film.

learn.title: Likes, plans and questions
learn.sub: Tap any word to hear it

blocks.title: A thing or an action
blocks.note: After aimer, a thing takes le, la or les: j'aime la musique, j'aime les frites. An action takes the infinitive: j'aime voyager, j'aime cuisiner.

blocks.text: After je vais, the next verb never changes. It stays as the infinitive: je vais manger, nous allons manger, ils vont manger. Only aller changes.
Est-ce que is only a way to start a question. Est-ce que tu aimes le café ? means the same as Tu aimes le café ? In writing and polite speech you will see est-ce que a lot.
To suggest something to friends, French uses on, not nous: on va au cinéma ? means shall we go to the cinema? You will hear pourquoi pas ?, why not, for yes.

phrases.es: Je vais regarder un film ce soir.
phrases.en: I'm going to watch a film tonight.
Shall we go to the cinema?

exercises.why: After je vais, use the infinitive: regarder.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means I'm going to eat?
exercises.why: Je vais plus the infinitive: je vais manger.

exercises.say: On va au cinéma ce soir ?
options: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?
Are we going to the café tonight?
exercises.why: On va au cinéma ? is shall we go to the cinema? Ce soir is tonight.

items.why: No form of aller: it is happening now.

items.text: Tu vas écouter de la musique.
items.full: Tu vas écouter de la musique.

exercises.why: A question word at the end is everyday French.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: After vais, use the infinitive: manger.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: After allons, use the infinitive: regarder.
Things you like take le, la or les: la musique.
Je vais plus the infinitive, and demain can go first or last.

exercises.q: To a friend: are you coming?
exercises.why: Tu viens ? with a rising voice is the everyday way to ask.
N'aime pas wraps the verb, and sport takes le.

exercises.prompt: I'm going to watch a film tonight.
exercises.answer: Je vais regarder un film ce soir.
exercises.why: Je vais, then the infinitive, then when.
For things you like in general, use le, la or les: la musique.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: On va au cinéma ? Who does on mean?
exercises.why: On is the everyday word for we.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Tell a friend one thing you like, and one thing you are going to do this weekend.
write.model: J'aime la musique et le cinéma. Ce week-end, je vais regarder un film.
checklist: J'aime with le, la or les for things
Je n'aime pas if you want to say you do not like something

boss.title: Making plans with Inès
boss.persona: You are Inès, a friendly French student who has become a friend of the learner. You are texting about the weekend. Talk about films, music, and plans for Saturday. Address the learner as tu. Keep every message to one short sentence.

turns.npc: Salut. Tu fais quoi ce week-end ?
turns.en: Hi. What are you doing this weekend?
choices: Je vais regarder un film. Et toi ?
Je regarder un film. Et toi ?
After je you need vais: je vais regarder.
Je vais regarde un film. Et toi ?
After vais, use the infinitive: regarder.

turns.en: Cool. Do you like the cinema?
choices: Oui, j'aime le cinéma.
Oui, j'aime cinéma.
Things you like take le, la or les: le cinéma.
Oui, j'aime du cinéma.
Du is for an amount. For things you like, use le: le cinéma.

turns.npc: Moi, j'adore ça. On va au cinéma samedi ?
turns.en: I love it. Shall we go to the cinema on Saturday?
choices: Pourquoi pas ? À quelle heure ?
Pourquoi pas ? À quel heure ?
Heure is feminine: quelle heure.
Pourquoi pas ? En quelle heure ?
At a time is à: à quelle heure ?

turns.npc: À huit heures ? Je vais réserver les billets.
turns.en: At eight? I'm going to book the tickets.
choices: D'accord. À samedi.
D'accord. À samedis.
Samedi has no s here: à samedi means see you Saturday.
D'accord. Au samedi.
See you Saturday is à samedi, with no le.

boss.chatOpening: Tu aimes quel genre de films ?
boss.chatOpeningEn: What kind of films do you like?
